diagnosis.answer: Obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with systolic anterior motion
accept: obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with systolic anterior motion

findings: Left ventricular hypertrophy with strain in lateral leads
Deep septal Q waves with left axis

echoTasks.find: Asymmetric septal thickening with a narrow outflow tract and systolic anterior motion with septal contact
Late peaking outflow gradient rising further with Valsalva and standing
Posteriorly directed late systolic jet from systolic anterior motion

auscultation.added: Fourth sound from the stiff ventricle
auscultation.murmur: Harsh late peaking systolic murmur grade 3 of 6 at the left sternal edge, louder with Valsalva and standing, softer with squatting

exam.general: Muscular 19 year old athlete, asymptomatic at rest, no distress
exam.other: Carotid pulse brisk with a spike and dome character, no oedema
exam.precordium: Sustained apex beat with a systolic thrill at the left sternal edge

history.a: One exertional faint during a kabaddi match last month, brief, full recovery
Occasional chest tightness on sprinting, no orthopnoea
Uncle died suddenly at 30 during sport, father has a murmur
No drugs, no supplements, no alcohol
State level kabaddi player, trains daily, selection trials next month
Screened at a camp after the faint, referred for echo

keyPoints: Restrict competitive sport immediately pending risk stratification, per the ACC and AHA hypertrophic cardiomyopathy guideline
Start a beta blocker to lower gradients and symptoms, with Holter, exercise test and family screening
Assess sudden death risk markers including wall thickness, aneurysm, arrhythmia and family history for defibrillator discussion
Refer to a cardiomyopathy centre for septal reduction assessment if gradients stay above 50 mmHg with symptoms
Screen first degree relatives with echo and ECG and counsel on genetics
management.model: Sport restriction with beta blockade, formal sudden death risk stratification, referral centre assessment, and family screening

sources: ACC and AHA guideline on hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, in own words
ASE chamber quantification guideline, in own words
stem: A 19 year old state level kabaddi player from Haryana faints during a match and is found to have a harsh late peaking murmur that grows with Valsalva and eases with squatting. There is a family history of sudden death in sport.
teaching: A murmur louder with Valsalva and softer with squatting is outflow obstruction physiology
Marked means resting or provoked gradient 50 mmHg or more, the septal reduction threshold
Systolic anterior motion with septal contact plus a posteriorly directed jet completes the mechanism
Exertional syncope with a family history of sudden death mandates restriction plus risk stratification
title: Obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in a young athlete
